sam: Quick question — for docs-only or image/asset updates, should deploy-bot auto-bump a patch and publish a release, or do we keep that manual? I hit a docs change that the tooling marked as a patch but I'm not sure we want a release note every tiny doc tweak.
olivia: I'm leaning manual. Docs churn can be noisy in release history. Maybe we auto-bump the package but don't create a release note unless `changelog:` present?
kai: +1 for auto-bump package version to avoid dep confusion, but suppress release notes by default. Could be an option: `--release-note=auto|manual|suppress`.
jen: We already have a `--changelog` flag on our release script. If deploy-bot set patch but the PR body includes a `changelog: none` line we can skip the public release note.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: detected commits: [docs/*.md, assets/*.svg], suggested action: create patch tag `v1.4.7` and skip changelog by default. Reaction :robot_face:. (run `./release --help` for override)
sam: That sounds reasonable. Two follow-ups: 1) what about pinned consumers that depend on semver semantics? 2) Should patch-only tags be annotated with `meta:docs` so downstream tooling can filter them?
marco: For pinned consumers, patch bump is semver-correct — shouldn't break anything. But customers who pin exact versions may get noisy updates; annotating tags is useful. We could use build metadata: `v1.4.7+docs.2026-02-12`.
olivia: I prefer a human-readable lightweight annotation: tag message "docs-only" or a tag suffix? Buildmeta is fine but some tools ignore it. What about adding an annotated git tag message `git tag -a v1.4.7 -m "docs-only: small copy tweak"`?
kai: Annotated tag plus lightweight release body is good. But keep changelog and release notes generators from listing them unless `changelog: include` in PR.
jen: Rollback question — if we later realize docs introduced a broken link causing customer confusion, do we do a patch revert that also bumps a patch? I'm thinking we should prefer a new patch bump (no force-retag) so history is linear.
sam: Agreed: avoid force-retag for any published tag. New patch bump for fixes. Add instruction to release docs.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: policy update proposed: "docs-only PRs => auto-patch-tag, annotated tag message 'docs-only', suppress release note unless PR contains 'changelog: include' or `--release-note` flag supplied." Use command `@deploy-bot apply-policy docs-only auto-patch suppress`.
marco: Can we also add a rule for assets-only (icons, svgs) vs localization? Locales sometimes affect strings exposed to customers and might deserve real changelog entries.
jen: Good point. Suggest rule: changes under `i18n/` or `locales/` default to manual review for changelog.
sam: OK let's capture this in the release playbook. I'll draft a short PR updating deploy-bot heuristics and the semver guidance: "patch for non-behavioral changes, never force-retag, annotate tags, release notes suppressed by default." 
olivia: :thumbsup: add example in playbook with `git tag -a` snippet and the deploy-bot override flags so folks know how to force a changelog entry.
kai: One more: CI should add a badge in the PR indicating "release: patch/docs-only" so reviewers see it. Small UX win to reduce back-and-forth.
sam: Great. I'll open the PR in 10m with proposed wording and a sample annotated tag command. Thanks all.
